pull.title: MINOR: Propagate ClusterInstance#deleteTopic errors and use it in more tests
pull.body:
Follow-up to #23699 to apply the same changes to
ClusterInstance#deleteTopic.

ClusterInstance#deleteTopic did not wait for the DeleteTopics result, so
a failed deletion (e.g. the topic did not exist) was either ignored or
hidden by the waitTopicDeletion timeout. It now calls get() and wraps
the cause in a RuntimeException, so callers no longer need to handle
ExecutionException and InterruptedException.

- Use ClusterInstance#deleteTopic in tests that delete a topic and then
immediately wait for the deletion.
- Rename ClusterTestExtensionsTest#testVerifyTopicDeletion to
testDeleteTopic and verify that deleting a non-existent topic fails with
UnknownTopicOrPartitionException.

Reviewers: Ken Huang <s7133700@gmail.com>, Chia-Ping Tsai
 <chia7712@gmail.com>

review_comments.body:
Personally, I don’t like to add those specific configurations since they look like something magic. Perhaps this PR can refactor that code as well.

1. ClusterInstance#deleteTopic should wait for metadata sync only
2. the logic of waiting disk sync could be moved to DeleteTopicTest. It is the only user
3. remove all those mysterious configurations from other test cases
Hmm, we already have https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21153 to handle that. This PR should wait until that is completed.

commit.message: Propagate ClusterInstance#deleteTopic errors and use it in more integration tests
Use kafka InterruptException instead of RuntimeException

Always wrap ExecutionException cause in ClusterInstance#deleteTopic

ApiException does not fill in its stack trace, so rethrowing it directly
hides the caller's location.
